subsystems.name: Surface laser spectrometer
subsystems.role: measures methane and its carbon-13 isotope in air samples taken by a rover.

subsystems.name: Orbital solar occultation spectrometer
subsystems.role: measures methane and other trace gases by looking at the Sun through the atmosphere at sunrise and sunset.

subsystems.name: Sample enrichment and handling
subsystems.role: concentrates methane from Martian air so the surface instrument can detect it.

subsystems.name: Calibration and reference system
subsystems.role: ensures measurements are accurate and comparable between instruments and over time.

subsystems.name: Data analysis and modelling
subsystems.role: separates real methane signals from instrument artefacts and atmospheric background.

buildSteps.title: Set the detection goal
buildSteps.detail: Instruments must find methane at parts-per-trillion and distinguish its carbon isotopes, so design starts from required sensitivity and spectral resolution.

buildSteps.title: Design the spectrometer
buildSteps.detail: Choose laser wavelengths or infrared bands that match methane absorption lines; for orbit, use solar occultation to get a long path through the atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate and align optics
buildSteps.detail: Build the laser or spectrometer, multi-pass cell and detectors, and align them to micron precision in a clean room.

buildSteps.title: Test in vacuum and thermal chambers
buildSteps.detail: Simulate space conditions, verify stability and calibration over expected temperature ranges.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate with known gases
buildSteps.detail: Use reference cells with known methane concentrations and isotopic ratios to establish accuracy.

buildSteps.title: Integrate onto the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: Mount on a rover or orbiter, connect power, data and thermal control.

buildSteps.title: Launch and commission
buildSteps.detail: After landing or orbit insertion, check out instrument performance in the real Martian environment.

buildSteps.title: Operate and collect data
buildSteps.detail: A rover ingests air and runs laser scans; an orbiter points at the Sun during sunrise and sunset to record absorption spectra.

buildSteps.title: Retrieve and interpret
buildSteps.detail: Convert spectra into methane concentrations and isotope ratios, cross-checking results between the surface and orbital measurements.

prerequisites.why: used in Earth monitoring and industrial sensing to detect trace gases at very low concentrations.
proven on Earth-orbiting and planetary missions to profile atmospheric gases.
needed to avoid contamination and to concentrate methane from thin Martian air.
especially for solar occultation, which requires precise tracking of the Sun through the atmosphere.

prerequisites.tech: Isotopic ratio measurement at trace levels
prerequisites.why: carbon-13 methane is extremely rare, so measuring its ratio pushes instrument limits.

prerequisites.tech: Understanding of Mars atmospheric chemistry and transport
prerequisites.why: models are still uncertain about how methane is destroyed and mixed, which affects interpretation.

pathway.milestone: NASA's Curiosity rover and ESA's ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter report different methane levels
pathway.unlocks: a live debate about sources, sinks and possible instrument artefacts.

pathway.milestone: future orbiters and rovers with improved sensitivity and spatial resolution
pathway.unlocks: better maps of where and when methane appears.

pathway.milestone: coordinated surface and orbital campaigns measuring the same regions at the same time
pathway.unlocks: distinguishing local sources from global background.

pathway.milestone: in-situ isotopic analysis of methane from a known source
pathway.unlocks: a definitive test of whether the methane is geological or biological.
